original_interpretation: TrendForce estimated the combined 2024 revenue of the world's top 10 OSAT companies at US$41.56 billion, up 3% year on year.
evidence_found: "The combined revenue of the world's top 10 OSAT companies reached US$41.56B in 2024, up 3% YoY." (TrendForce press release, 13 May 2025, re-opened 2026-09-30)
notes: Figure, unit, period and growth match. TrendForce does not disclose whether ASE revenue includes EMS; population caveat in metric is honest. No 2025 TrendForce OSAT ranking found as of 2026-09-30.

original_interpretation: TrendForce ranked ASE first among OSATs in 2024 with revenue of US$18.54 billion, nearly 45% of the top-10 total.
evidence_found: ASE: "$18.54B, holding nearly a 45% share among the top ten" (TrendForce press release, 13 May 2025, re-opened 2026-09-30)
notes: 18.54/41.56 = 44.6%, consistent with "nearly 45%".

original_interpretation: TrendForce ranked Amkor second among OSATs in 2024 with revenue of US$6.32 billion, down 2.8% year on year.
evidence_found: Amkor "ranked second with $6.32B in revenue (-2.8% YoY)" (TrendForce press release, 13 May 2025, re-opened 2026-09-30)

original_interpretation: TrendForce ranked JCET third among OSATs in 2024 with revenue of US$5.0 billion, up 19.3% year on year.
evidence_found: JCET "took third place with $5B in revenue (+19.3% YoY)" (TrendForce press release, 13 May 2025, re-opened 2026-09-30)

original_interpretation: TrendForce ranked Tongfu Microelectronics fourth among OSATs in 2024 with revenue of US$3.32 billion, up 5.6% year on year.
evidence_found: "Fourth-ranked Tongfu Microelectronics recorded $3.32B in revenue (+5.6% YoY)" (TrendForce press release, 13 May 2025, re-opened 2026-09-30)

original_interpretation: TrendForce ranked Powertech Technology fifth among OSATs in 2024 with revenue of US$2.28 billion, up 1% year on year.
evidence_found: Powertech Technology "came in fifth with $2.28B in revenue (+1% YoY)" (TrendForce press release, 13 May 2025, re-opened 2026-09-30)

original_interpretation: TrendForce ranked HT-Tech (Tianshui Huatian) sixth among OSATs in 2024 with revenue of US$2.01 billion, up 26% year on year.
evidence_found: HT-Tech sixth, "$2.01B in revenue (+26% YoY)" (TrendForce press release, 13 May 2025, re-opened 2026-09-30)

original_interpretation: TrendForce ranked WiseRoad seventh (US$1.56bn, +5%), Hana Micron eighth (US$0.92bn, +23.7%), KYEC ninth (US$0.91bn, -14.5%) and ChipMOS tenth (US$0.71bn, +3.1%) among OSATs by 2024 revenue.
evidence_found: WiseRoad 7th "$1.56B in revenue (+5% YoY)"; Hana Micron 8th "$920M in revenue (+23.7% YoY)"; KYEC 9th "$910M in revenue (-14.5% YoY)"; ChipMOS 10th "$710M in revenue (+3.1% YoY)" (TrendForce press release, 13 May 2025, re-opened 2026-09-30)
notes: All four ranks, values and growth rates match. Claim bundles four figures; not atomic but accurate.

original_interpretation: TrendForce attributed the double-digit 2024 revenue growth of Chinese OSATs such as JCET and HT-Tech to government policy support and domestic demand.
evidence_found: "OSAT providers from China, such as JCET and HT-Tech, saw strong double-digit revenue growth—supported by government policies and domestic demand—posing a growing challenge to the existing market order." (TrendForce press release, 13 May 2025, re-opened 2026-09-30)
notes: Supported as TrendForce's attribution. claim_type "estimate" is a loose fit: this is an analyst's causal interpretation, not a modelled figure; readers should treat the causality as TrendForce's opinion.

original_interpretation: DIGITIMES Research estimated global OSAT revenue at US$41.2 billion in 2024, up 5% from 2023.
evidence_found: "global OSAT revenue reached US$41.2 billion in 2024, a 5% increase from the previous year" (DIGITIMES Research, "Global OSAT industry, 2025", published 20 Aug 2025; public abstract, full report paywalled)
notes: Source page titles the report "Global OSAT industry, 2025". Definition/coverage not disclosed in the public portion, as the claim metric already states.

original_interpretation: TrendForce's US$18.54bn for ASE in 2024 appears to be ASE's whole consolidated revenue including its EMS business (about 40% of revenue), so the top-10 OSAT total overstates pure assembly-and-test revenue.
evidence_found: Checked inputs: CLM-0240 (ASE FY2025 NT$645,388m, +8.4%) implies FY2024 ~NT$595.4bn; independent search results report ASE 2024 revenue of NT$595.41bn (+2.3%). At a 2024 average of roughly NT$32.1/US$, 595.41/32.1 = US$18.5bn, matching TrendForce's "$18.54B" for ASE (SRC-0331). CLM-0535 gives EMS at ~40% of 2025 revenue.
correction: Arithmetic holds: TrendForce's ASE figure matches ASE's full consolidated revenue, so it almost certainly includes EMS (and ISE Labs/SPIL). The EMS ~40% share cited is for 2025 (CLM-0535), not 2024; the 2024 EMS share was not checked here. The exchange rate is approximate and not taken from an ASE filing.
notes: Inference is sound but rests on unverified inputs CLM-0240 and CLM-0535 and an approximate FX rate; TrendForce itself does not state what ASE revenue it used.

original_interpretation: Because TrendForce's top-10 OSAT total (US$41.56bn) exceeds DIGITIMES Research's whole-market OSAT revenue (US$41.2bn) for the same year, the two publishers must define OSAT revenue differently (likely including vs excluding ASE's EMS revenue).
evidence_found: Re-checked both inputs: TrendForce top-10 total "US$41.56B in 2024" (SRC-0331) and DIGITIMES "global OSAT revenue reached US$41.2 billion in 2024" (SRC-0332). Growth rates also differ (+3% vs +5%).
notes: Logic is valid: a top-10 subset cannot exceed a whole market measured on the same basis, so the bases differ. The EMS explanation is flagged as "likely", appropriately; other possible differences (FX rates, test-only houses, company scope) remain. Already captured in CON-0031.

original_interpretation: Yole Group estimated the advanced packaging market at US$46 billion in 2024, up 19% year on year after the 2023 downturn.
evidence_found: "Advanced packaging market reached $46 billion in 2024, up 19% YoY after the 2023 downturn." (Yole Group release republished by Edge AI and Vision Alliance, 2 Sep 2025)
notes: Republication of a Yole release on an industry-press site; original yolegroup.com release not opened. No newer Yole annual figure found publicly (Yole Q1 2026 monitor page returned 403; search snippets mention Q4 2025 quarterly AP revenue of nearly $15B but no full-year 2025 total).

original_interpretation: Yole Group forecast the advanced packaging market to exceed US$79.4 billion by 2030, a 9.5% CAGR over 2024-2030.
evidence_found: "Market projected to exceed $79.4 billion by 2030, with a CAGR2024-2030 of 9.5%" (Yole Group release republished by Edge AI and Vision Alliance, 2 Sep 2025); Microwave Journal (SRC-0334): "With revenues expected to reach $79.4 billion by 2030" (no CAGR stated there).
notes: Forecast correctly labelled as estimate. SRC-0334 corroborates the $79.4bn but not the 9.5% CAGR; both are republications of the same Yole release, so not independent corroboration. No newer Yole long-range forecast found publicly as of 2026-09-30.

original_interpretation: Yole Group estimated that mobile and consumer electronics accounted for about 70% of 2024 advanced packaging revenue, while telecom and infrastructure is the fastest-growing segment at a 14.9% CAGR for 2024-2030.
evidence_found: "Mobile & consumer electronics remains the largest market, accounting for ~70% of 2024 revenues."; "Telecom & infrastructure is the fastest-growing segment with a +14.9% CAGR between 2024 and 2030" (Yole Group release republished by Edge AI and Vision Alliance, 2 Sep 2025)
notes: The 14.9% is a forecast CAGR; claim wording "is the fastest-growing segment" should be read as forecast.

original_interpretation: Yole Group's 2024 advanced packaging player ranking is led by IDMs (Intel, Sony, Samsung, YMTC and SK hynix), followed by OSATs and foundries such as TSMC.
evidence_found: "IDMs lead the market with Intel, Sony, Samsung, YMTC, and SK Hynix, followed by OSATs and the leading foundry TSMC." (Yole Group release republished by Edge AI and Vision Alliance, 2 Sep 2025); Microwave Journal: "The 2024 ranking of advanced packaging players highlights a shifting landscape: IDMs dominate with Intel, Sony, Samsung, YMTC and SK Hynix leading, followed by OSATs and foundries such as TSMC."
notes: Ranking basis not stated in either republication. The researcher note explaining why YMTC/Sony appear (hybrid bonding) is speculation not in the source.

original_interpretation: Yole Group reported Chinese OSAT advanced-packaging investments: JCET US$1.5 billion, HT-Tech a second-phase expansion of 10 billion yuan (about US$1.4bn) and Tongfu a 7.5 billion yuan (about US$1.0bn) project.
evidence_found: "JCET announced a $1.5 billion investment"; "HT-Tech launched a second-phase expansion worth 10 billion yuan, about $1.4 billion"; "Tongfu Microelectronics announced a 7.5 billion yuan (~$1.0 billion) advanced packaging project" (Yole Group release republished by Edge AI and Vision Alliance, 2 Sep 2025)
notes: Correctly typed as reported_claim: these are company announcements relayed by Yole; announced investments, not spent capex. Announcement dates not given.

original_interpretation: Yole Group estimated that in 2023 the advanced packaging market was worth about US$38 billion, 44% of the total IC packaging market.
evidence_found: "In 2023, when the advanced packaging market was worth about US$38 billion, it was 44 percent of the total IC packaging market." (eeNews Europe, 29 Jul 2024, reporting Yole)
notes: Consistent with Yole's 2025 release (2024 = $46bn, +19% YoY implies 2023 of ~$38.7bn). Press report of Yole, not Yole directly.

original_interpretation: In mid-2024 Yole Group forecast the advanced packaging market at about US$42.5 billion for 2024 and US$47.5 billion for 2025, reaching about US$69.5 billion in 2029 (11% CAGR 2023-2029).
evidence_found: "The advanced packaging market will be worth about US$42.5 billion in 2024 and US$47.5 billion in 2025."; "Over the period 2023 to 2029 the annual market is expected to have a compound annual growth rate of 11 percent and be worth about US$69.5 billion in 2029." (eeNews Europe, 29 Jul 2024, reporting Yole)
correction: Accurately recorded as a mid-2024 forecast, but superseded: Yole's September 2025 release puts actual 2024 advanced packaging revenue at US$46bn (+19% YoY), not US$42.5bn, and now forecasts over US$79.4bn by 2030 at a 9.5% CAGR 2024-2030 (CLM-1029, CLM-1030). Do not use the US$42.5bn figure as the 2024 market size.
notes: See CON-0032.

original_interpretation: Yole's 2023 figures imply a total IC packaging market of roughly US$86 billion in 2023 (US$38bn advanced at 44% share), of which traditional packaging was roughly US$48 billion.
evidence_found: Inputs re-checked in SRC-0335: "about US$38 billion", "44 percent of the total IC packaging market". 38/0.44 = 86.36; 86.36 - 38 = 48.36.
notes: Arithmetic correct; inputs are rounded so the implied totals carry roughly +/-US$2bn uncertainty. Scope (in-house plus outsourced) caveat is appropriate.

original_interpretation: CSET put the 2019 in-house assembly, test and packaging market (performed by foundries and IDMs such as Intel, Samsung, SK hynix, Micron and TSMC) at about US$25 billion, versus US$28 billion for OSATs.
evidence_found: Table 4 "ATP Sectors, Market Size, and Leading Firms", column "2019 Market Size": "Outsourced semiconductor assembly and test $28 billion"; "In-house ATP (by foundries and IDMs) $25 billion Intel (USA), Samsung (USA), S.K. Hynix (South Korea), Micron (USA), TSMC (Taiwan), others"; "Source: Khan, Mann, and Peterson, \"The Semiconductor Supply Chain,\" 24." (printed p. 16) SRC-0201
notes: CSET itself mislabels Samsung as USA-headquartered in this table; irrelevant to the figures.

original_interpretation: On CSET's 2019 figures, OSATs performed a little over half (about 53%) of the value of global assembly, test and packaging, with IDMs and foundries doing about 47% in-house.
evidence_found: Inputs re-checked in Table 4 (printed p. 16): OSAT $28 billion, in-house ATP $25 billion (2019). 28/53 = 52.8%.
notes: Arithmetic correct. The measurement caveat in notes (in-house ATP has no market price) is appropriate; CSET does not explain how the in-house value was estimated.

original_interpretation: CSET reported that semiconductor makers began establishing assembly factories in Asia as early as the 1960s to take advantage of low labour rates, and that ATP has traditionally been viewed as labour-intensive and low-margin.
evidence_found: "companies have traditionally viewed the process of assembly, test, and packaging as a labor-intensive and low-margin activity"; "Beginning as early as the 1960s, semiconductor manufacturers established factories in Asia to take advantage of low labor rates." (printed p. 12, citing VerWey) SRC-0201
notes: Text matches. claim_type "fact" from a tier-2 think-tank source: acceptable for a well-documented historical statement, but the "low-margin" view is a characterisation, not a measured fact.

original_interpretation: CSET estimated back-end ATP at about 10% of the value of a finished chip, while SIA/BCG estimated 6% of value added, 3% of industry R&D and 13% of industry capital expenditure.
evidence_found: "An earlier CSET report calculated that back-end ATP represented ~10 percent of the value of a finished chip, compared with roughly 45 percent value added by the design and front-end fabrication steps." (printed p. 11); "estimating that ATP contributes 6 percent of a chip's value, while the overall industry segment is responsible for 3 percent of industry research and development (R&D) and 13 percent of industry capital expenditures." (printed pp. 11-12) SRC-0201
notes: CSET frames the SIA/BCG figure as "6 percent of a chip's value" and says SIA/BCG "shares this finding"; the claim's "value added" wording is close enough.

original_interpretation: CSET, citing a 2021 industry estimate, counted packaging facilities as China 114, Taiwan 106, rest of Asia-Pacific 65, North America 35, Japan 27 and Europe 19.
evidence_found: "Recent estimates suggest China leads in the overall number of packaging facilities (114), followed by Taiwan (106), the rest of the Asia-Pacific (65), North America (35), Japan (27), and Europe (19)." (printed p. 15, footnote 31: Lapedus, "Expanding Advanced Packaging Production in the U.S.", Semiconductor Engineering) SRC-0201
notes: CSET says "Recent estimates", citing a Semiconductor Engineering article; the "2021" date in the claim comes from that article's vintage, not stated in the sentence itself. Counts are unweighted by size.

original_interpretation: CSET (citing Yole) reported that in 2020 the top 10 advanced-packaging firms held 93% of advanced packaging capacity, with capacity by firm headquarters of Taiwan 48%, United States 22%, China 14% and South Korea 9%.
evidence_found: "As of 2020, the top 10 leading firms engaged in advanced packaging accounted for 93 percent of all advanced packaging capacity. These 10 firms are located in Taiwan (48 percent of all capacity), the United States (22 percent), China (14 percent), and South Korea (9 percent)." (Appendix, printed p. 29; Figure A "Advanced Packaging 2020 Wafer Split by Country (300 mm equivalent)") SRC-0201
notes: The 48/22/14/9 shares are of ALL advanced packaging capacity (they sum to the 93% held by the top 10), not of the top-10 firms' capacity as the metric population implies. The appendix paragraph carries no footnote; the Yole attribution rests on nearby citations (Kumar, Chitoraga and Shoo 2021).

original_interpretation: By 2020 advanced-packaging wafer volume, ASE held 26%, TSMC 15%, Samsung 6%, Chipbond 5%, Nepes 3% and ChipMOS 2% (CSET citing Yole).
evidence_found: "Taiwan's ASE Group (26 percent), TSMC (15 percent), Chipbond (5 percent), and ChipMOS (2 percent) are all among the top 10 firms in 2020, when measured by advanced packaging wafers. South Korea's Samsung (6 percent) and Nepes (3 percent) are also among the top 10." (printed p. 32, footnote 80: Kumar, Chitoraga, and Shoo, "Status of the Advanced Packaging Industry 2021," 66) SRC-0201

original_interpretation: CSET (citing Yole) reported 2020 advanced-packaging capex of Intel US$3.5bn (32%), TSMC US$2.8bn (25%), ASE US$2.0bn (18%), Samsung US$1.5bn (14%), Amkor US$0.7bn (6%) and JCET US$0.5bn (5%).
evidence_found: Table A "2020 Leading Advanced Packaging Capital Expenditures": "Intel United States 3.5 32%", "TSMC Taiwan 2.8 25%", "ASE Group Taiwan 2 18%", "Samsung S. Korea 1.5 14%", "Amkor United States 0.7 6%", "JCET China 0.5 5%"; "Source: Kumar, Chitoraga, and Shoo, \"Status of the Advanced Packaging Industry 2021,\" 236." (printed p. 30) SRC-0201
notes: Percentages are CSET/Yole's "AP CapEx Split" among these six firms (they sum to 100%), not shares of total industry AP capex.

original_interpretation: CSET, citing Yole, reported the overall packaging market at US$53.2 billion in 2014 with advanced packaging US$20.2 billion (38%), and projected US$96.1 billion in 2024 with advanced packaging US$48.2 billion (50%).
evidence_found: "The overall packaging market's value in 2014 stood at $53.2 billion, with advanced packaging accounting for $20.2 billion (38 percent) of that total. By 2024, estimates suggest the overall packaging market's value will be around $96.1 billion, with advanced packaging accounting for $48.2 billion (50 percent) of that total." (printed pp. 9-10, footnote 10: Kumar, Chitoraga, and Shoo, Yole 2021) SRC-0201
correction: 2014 figures verified as recorded. The 2024 projection (US$96.1bn total, US$48.2bn advanced, 50%) was a 2021 forecast and is superseded: Yole's September 2025 release estimates actual 2024 advanced packaging revenue at US$46bn (CLM-1029), and Yole's mid-2024 data put advanced packaging at 44% of IC packaging in 2023 (CLM-1034). Use the 2024 projection only as a historical forecast.

original_interpretation: CSET (citing Yole) reported that 19% of wafers went to advanced packaging and 81% to conventional packaging in 2014, with analysts expecting a 35%/65% split by 2026; an advanced-packaged wafer is worth about double a conventionally packaged one.
evidence_found: "the number of wafers destined for advanced packaging as opposed to conventional packaging (the \"wafer split\") stood at 19 percent versus 81 percent in 2014 ... By 2026, analysts anticipate that the wafer split between advanced and traditional packaging will be 35 percent versus 65 percent."; "the value of an advanced packaging wafer is double that of a traditionally packaged wafer, resulting in a high profit margin for manufacturers." (printed p. 10, footnotes 12-13: Yole 2021, p. 30) SRC-0201
notes: The 2026 split is a 2021 forecast; no public actual for 2026 found. "Double the value" is a Yole/CSET generalisation.

original_interpretation: In Yole's 2020 advanced-packaging wafer split, fan-in wafer-level packaging accounted for 48% of wafers and flip-chip (FC-CSP/FC-BGA) 43%, while 2.5D/3D stacking was 5% and fan-out 4%.
evidence_found: Table 1 "Types of Advanced Packaging Technologies" (printed p. 9; source Kumar, Chitoraga and Shoo 2021, p. 36): FC-CSP/FC-BGA "43% 8%"; 2D, 2.5D, 3D Stacking "N/A 5% 15%"; FO-WLP "4% 15%"; FO-PLP CAGR "12%"; FI-WLP "48% 5%"; Embedded Die/SiP "N/A <1% 23%" (columns: advanced packaging wafer split 2020; wafer split CAGR 2019-25). SRC-0201
notes: Shares sum to ~100% of advanced-packaging wafers. The claim omits embedded die/SiP (<1%), which is fine.

original_interpretation: CSET reported (citing Yole) that mobile and consumer accounted for 71% of advanced packaging revenue in 2020, telecom and infrastructure 20% and automotive and transportation 7%.
evidence_found: "Mobile and consumer accounted for 71 percent of the advanced packaging market by revenue in 2020, followed by telecommunications and infrastructure (20 percent) and automotive and transportation (7 percent)." (printed p. 10, footnote 14: Kumar, Chitoraga, and Shoo, Yole 2021, p. 34) SRC-0201
notes: Consistent with Yole's ~70% mobile & consumer share in 2024 (CLM-1031).

original_interpretation: CSET reported that the ten largest OSAT firms by revenue were headquartered in mainland China (3), Taiwan (5) and Singapore (1), with major factories also in the Philippines and Malaysia.
evidence_found: "Today, 9 of the 10 largest OSAT firms by revenue are headquartered in mainland China (3), Taiwan (5), and Singapore (1)." (printed p. 31, footnote 77: Yole 2021, p. 70); "leading OSAT firms have a notable physical presence (i.e., factories) in countries such as the Philippines and Malaysia." (printed p. 32) SRC-0201
correction: CSET says 9 of the 10 largest OSATs (not "the ten largest") are headquartered in mainland China (3), Taiwan (5) and Singapore (1). CSET does not name the tenth firm; that it is Amkor (US) is the researcher's inference, not in the source. The ranking is Yole's 2021-vintage data, not current; TrendForce's 2024 top 10 (SRC-0331) has no Singapore firm and includes South Korea's Hana Micron.
notes: Superseding corrected claim added in this batch.
